sentences.text: By way of this application, filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the applicant - Piraram @ Piyush Darji is seeking regular bail in connection with the FIR being C.R.No.11191005211303 of 2021 registered with Khadia Police Station, Ahmedabad for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 306, 323, 294B and 114 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 and 7 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
2. The Trial Court, by its order dated 04.04.2022, declined to grant the prayer of regular bail made by the applicant- accused.
Dissatisfied with the order, the applicant has preferred instant application.

3. Facts and circumstances giving rise to file present bail application are that the wife of the applicant ended her life NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/10399/2022 ORDER DATED:
Piraram @ Piyush Bansilal Darji vs State Of Gujarat on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84107835/
1 20/01/2023 undefined by committing suicide at her matrimonial home.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The marriage of the deceased with the present applicant was solemnized on 29.06.2020.
The incident of suicide took place on 21.10.2021.
On 24.10.2021, the applicant herein arrested pursuant to the FIR lodged by the brother of the deceased.
It is the case of the prosecution that after the marriage, deceased was denied to pursue competitive exam so as to enable her to join the government or banking service.
It is alleged that the present applicant and the in- laws of the deceased demanded Rs.1 lakh towards the dowry and accordingly, it was paid by the father of the deceased.

It is alleged that when deceased was pregnant, the husband - applicant said her that the child conceived is not of his child, but it is someone who conceived her, and thereby, the applicant was suspected on her character.
It is alleged that after birth of the baby-boy, the applicant-husband maintained extramarital affairs relationship and ignored the presence of the deceased.
It is alleged that the deceased was subjected to mental and physical torture and cruelty, as a result of which, she had left her with no other alternative but put an end to her life.
She committed suicide by hanging herself at her NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/10399/2022 ORDER DATED: 20/01/2023 undefined matrimonial home.
The brother of the deceased lodged an FIR against the applicant and in-laws.

The Investigating Officer of the case,
after competition of the investigation, submitted chargesheet before the Court concerned and same has been culminated into Sessions Case No.31 of 2022.

4. This Court has heard learned counsel Mr.Zubin Bharda with learned advocate Mr.Kishan H.
Dahiya, appearing for and on behalf of the applicant-accused, Mr.R.J. Goswami, learned counsel for original informant and Ms.Moxa Thakkar, learned APP for the respondent-State.
5.
Mr.Bharda, learned counsel for the applicant - accused would submit that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the alleged offence.

He would further urge that looking to the FIR and statements of witnesses, nothing has been brought on record to suggest that the applicant - accused had provoked incited or induced the deceased to commit suicide.

He would further submit that the allegations against the applicant that he was suspecting on the character of the deceased and having extramarital relationship with someone, are far from the truth as except bald allegations, nothing has been brought NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/10399/2022 ORDER DATED: 20/01/2023 undefined on record to establish the allegations, as referred in the FIR.

In support his contentions,
strong reliance has been placed on the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of K.V. Prakash Babu Vs. State of Karnataka (AIR 2016 SC 5430) to submit that extramarital relationship per se, or as such would not come within the ambit of Section 498A of the IPC.

entities.text: K.V. Prakash Babu Vs. State of Karnataka (AIR 2016 SC 5430)

sentences.text: 6. Mr.Bharda, learned advocate would further submit that looking to the FIR and chargesheet case papers, accepted as it is, then also no offence as alleged under Section 306 of the IPC made out against the applicant and therefore, the facts and circumstances of the case do not in any way indicate that the alleged act and/or allegation would constitute abetment to commit suicide and there is a complete absence of any sort of instigation or any positive act on the part of the applicant-accused, leading to the deceased to commit suicide.
On the factual facts, it is submitted that after pregnancy, the social gathering was held at the matrimonial home and everyone was happy including the deceased.

To substantiate the contentions, heavy reliance is being placed on the photographs of the function to submit that there was no any issue as alleged NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/10399/2022 ORDER DATED: 20/01/2023 undefined in the FIR.

On the issue of Piraram @ Piyush Bansilal Darji vs State Of Gujarat on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84107835/
2 maintaining extramarital relationship, he submitted that the applicant was working as a nursing staff with the private hospital, where other lady staff members were working with him and being a staff member, they were invited in the social gathering, which clearly shows that the false allegation having been alleged by brother of the deceased.
7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mr.Bharda, learned advocate would further submit that the applicant is in custody since 24.10.2021 and he having a responsibility to feed the family and trial would take considerable time and therefore, keeping the applicant behind the bar would serve no further purpose.
Thus, he prays that discretion may kindly be exercised in favour of the applicant.

8. On the other hand, Ms.Moxa Thakkar, learned APP for the respondent - State and Mr.R.J.
Goswami, learned advocate for the original informant vehemently opposed the bail application and contended that there is a reasonable ground to believe that the accused has committed the offence.

It is submitted that at the relevant time, deceased was having a mother child aged about five months and therefore, despite the mother of child, she took drastic NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/10399/2022 ORDER DATED: 20/01/2023 undefined steps to end her life which facts sufficient to infer that husband and his relatives abetted the alleged suicide.
It is further submitted that the issue raised by the applicant cannot be appreciated at this stage as it is to be tried by the Trial Court.
In such circumstances, it is prayed that no case is made out for exercising judicial discretion.

9. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, it is admitted fact that within short span of time of the marriage, the deceased committed a suicide leaving behind five months' old child.
As per the prosecution case, the applicant-accused being husband having suspicion on the character of the deceased and he was in extramarital relationship.

In such circumstances, considering the contents of the FIR and chargesheet case papers, this Court is of the prima facie view that there is a reasonable ground to believe that the accused has committed the offence.
Where prima facie case is made out and the offences grave, the Court would not enlarge the applicant- accused on bail.
The act of the suicide is within the seven years of the marriage.
It is settled proposition of law that in the case of abetment of suicide, the instigation has to be gathered from the circumstances of the case.
In all cases, NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/10399/2022 ORDER DATED: 20/01/2023 undefined there may not be a direct evidence with regard to the instigation.
In such circumstances, doubting the character of the wife and allegation of maintaining extramarital relationship, which are the prime factors, led to the deceased to commit the suicide.

In such circumstances, this Court is of the opinion that the contentions canvassed by counsel for the applicant should not be examined on merits by appreciation of evidence as it would be the trail Court to consider and appreciate the evidence.

10. For the foregoing reasons and considering the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case,
without discussion on merits of the case, the present case is not a fit case where judicial discretion to admit the applicant on bail required to be exercised and therefore, the application deserves dismissal and accordingly dismissed.
Rule is discharged.
